statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is at least 2
s has exactly n minus 1 entries
each entry of s is either plus 1 or minus 1
a is a permutation of the set {1, 2, ..., n}
the entries a1 through an are all distinct and each lies in {1, 2, ..., n}
the inequality condition is required for every index i from 1 to n minus 1
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each fixed integer n at least 2, consider all sign sequences of length n minus 1 with entries plus or minus 1. Define f(s) as the number of permutations of {1, 2, ..., n} whose consecutive differences have the prescribed signs. The task is to identify exactly which sign sequences s maximize f(s).
quantifier_order: For each integer n with n at least 2
For each sign sequence s of length n minus 1
Count all permutations a of {1, 2, ..., n} satisfying the adjacent sign constraints for every index i from 1 to n minus 1
Determine which sign sequences s maximize this count f(s)

variables.name: n
variables.role: fixed parameter with n at least 2

variables.domain: sequences of length n minus 1 with entries in plus or minus 1
variables.name: s
variables.role: parameter over which the maximization is taken

variables.name: i
variables.role: index for adjacent comparisons in the sign sequence and permutation

variables.name: a
variables.role: counted object satisfying the sign constraints

witness_dependencies: The counted permutation a depends on the chosen n and sign sequence s
The maximality question is over s for each fixed n
There is no existential witness in the statement, only a counting definition and a maximization problem
